subject: Data sovereignty & retention questions for CloudMarket listing — AWS/GCP/Azure
messages:
From: CloudMarket Partner Team <partners@cloudmarket.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>
Cc: AWS Marketplace Ops <marketplace-aws@amazon.com>
Date: Fri, 20 Mar 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Questions: residency & retention for our CloudMarket listing

Hi Soojin,

Thanks again for the quick demo last week — CloudMarket is excited to list Redwood on our multi-cloud marketplace. Before we move to the technical review, two compliance items came up from our legal/security team and from AWS Marketplace ops. Would you help clarify?

1) Data residency: For customers that request tenant-data to remain in a specific jurisdiction (e.g., AWS us-east-1 vs GCP europe-west1), can Redwood pin data storage and inference execution to a single cloud provider and region per customer when running through the marketplace offering?

2) Retention & deletion: What is Redwood's standard data retention policy for marketplace-deployed customers, and do you support a programmatic deletion endpoint and audit-proof deletion confirmation (for procurement evidence)?

3) Cross-cloud metadata: If logs or billing metadata need to cross regions for billing/observability, can that be disabled for regulated customers?

We copied AWS ops and attached the residency matrix they requested in their template. If you can respond with a short Q&A and any artifacts (SOC2, short flow for deletion, or sample contract language), we can proceed to the listing checklist.

Appreciate it,
— CloudMarket Partner Team

[attachments: partner-residency-template.xlsx]

From: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>
To: CloudMarket Partner Team <partners@cloudmarket.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Mateo Alvarez <mateo.alvarez@redwood.ai>, AWS Marketplace Ops <marketplace-aws@amazon.com>
Date: Fri, 20 Mar 2026 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Questions: residency & retention for our CloudMarket listing

Hi — thanks for the clear list. Looping in Marissa (product) and Mateo (security) to provide definitive answers and artifacts. High-level answers below and we will follow with a short consolidated Q&A doc and the requested attachments.

High-level:
- Residency: Yes — Redwood supports pinning both storage and inference execution to a specific region and cloud for a given customer when we run in Dedicated or Private modes. For the hosted Marketplace integration we have two supported options: 1) a region-scoped offering (single cloud/region) or 2) cross-region offering (multi-cloud routing). We recommend the region-scoped option for regulated customers.
- Retention & deletion: Standard retention for inference request logs is 30 days by default, extendable with a contract. We provide an API for deletion and can emit a signed deletion confirmation (audit artifact). For Marketplace customers we can also include a contractual retention floor and deletion SLA.
- Cross-cloud metadata: We can disable cross-cloud billing/observability exports for customers that require strict residency; billing events can be kept in-region or forwarded only to a customer-controlled endpoint.

Action items from Redwood:
1) Mateo to confirm technical controls and provide the deletion flow diagram + audit artifact template (attachment).
2) Marissa to prepare suggested contract language for the CloudMarket listing and marketplace checklist annotations.
3) I'll assemble a short Q&A PDF and SOC2/attestation links.

Will follow up with attachments within EOD today.

Thanks,
Soojin

From: Mateo Alvarez <mateo.alvarez@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Questions: residency & retention for our CloudMarket listing

Thanks for pulling this together. Quick technical clarifications from security/runtime: 

1) Execution residency: On Dedicated and Private we run inference on customer-provisioned or Redwood-allocated GPU hosts inside the requested region (AWS/GCP/Azure). For the hosted marketplace flow we can provision region-scoped runtime pools (e.g., us-east-1 on AWS) and tag the customer so routing is locked to that pool. We do not replicate inference KV cache or user prompts across regions for region-locked customers.

2) Storage residency: Customer artifacts (prompts, attachments, logs) can be configured to persist in a region-scoped object store (S3/GCS/Azure Blob). For Marketplace listings we offer an option to 1) hold data in Redwood-managed regional buckets, 2) forward raw logs to customer-managed buckets (recommended for strict residency), or 3) encrypt and envelope keys such that keys remain customer-managed (KMS/HSM).

3) Deletion & audit trail: We provide a programmatic deletion API (/v1/customers/{id}/data:delete) that triggers the following: pre-delete snapshot, delete objects from region-scoped store, scrub KV cache, and mark deletion in our audit ledger. We will return a signed deletion receipt containing object counts and timestamps. For immutable backups we have a 30-day backup retention which can be shortened via contract; deletion requests will cascade to backups after retention window ends unless contract requires immediate purging (we can provide contract language for this).

4) Logs/metadata: Operational logs that are strictly required for infrastructure health can optionally be redacted or kept in-region. Billing metering can be exported to customer-controlled endpoints to avoid cross-region exports.

Attached: redwood-data-residency-matrix.pdf and retention-delete-flowchart.png.

If CloudMarket needs us to meet any specific Marketplace technical checklist items, point us at the doc and we'll annotate.

— Mateo
Mateo Alvarez
Security & Infrastructure Engineering | Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Questions: residency & retention for our CloudMarket listing

Hi all — attaching suggested contract snippets and marketplace checklist annotations (see aws-marketplace-requirements-annotated.docx). Key items to consider including in the CloudMarket listing and subscriber T&Cs: 

- Residency guarantee: "Redwood will restrict processing and storage of Customer Data to the cloud region(s) and provider(s) specified in the Order. Redwood will not transfer Customer Data outside the specified region(s) except as authorized in writing."
- Retention & deletion SLA: "Redwood will retain request data for a maximum of X days (default 30) unless otherwise specified. Upon Customer request, Redwood will delete Customer Data and provide a signed deletion receipt within Y business days."
- Backup handling: "Backups are covered by the retention policy, and deletion requests will be honored for primary and backup stores as per the agreed retention window; exceptions must be negotiated."
- Audit evidence: reference to signed deletion receipt, KMS key policies, and SOC2 report URL or redacted attestation.

Next steps: CloudMarket — if you confirm the region-scoped listing option and your required retention floors, we'll prepare final contract language and a short onboarding checklist for your buyers.

Best,
Marissa
Marissa Cole
Product Manager, Enterprise Integrations | Redwood Inference

Thanks — this is exactly what we needed. Quick confirmations: 

- We will proceed with the region-scoped AWS listing (us-east-1) for regulated customers.
- Retention floor: we will list default 30 days but include an optional contract addendum to shorten to 7 days for certain customers.
- Please add the signed deletion receipt flow to the onboarding checklist and include KMS key controls as an option for customers wishing to manage keys.

Attachments received and we will flag a couple of buyers to verify KMS options during procurement. AWS Marketplace ops, please let us know if any of this needs further annotation on your side.

Appreciate the fast turnaround — looking forward to the listing.

— CloudMarket Partner Team
